claims.explanation: SB-216641 is a 5-HT1B/1D antagonist, and its selective killing pattern is best explained by dependence on serotonin receptor signaling, particularly HTR1B expression, which may drive autocrine survival or MAPK/PI3K crosstalk in sensitive lineages. TP53 mutation is nearly universal in both sensitive and resistant lines, so it is not predictive; instead, sensitivity is associated with mutations that activate the PI3K/AKT/mTOR and MAPK pathways (e.g., PIK3CA, PTEN loss, BRAF, NF1 loss, MET, EGFR) and with high HTR1B expression, while resistance is linked to EGFR-mutant lung lines and certain mesenchymal/neuroendocrine lineages.

features.basis: SB-216641 is a selective HTR1B antagonist; high receptor expression may indicate dependence on 5-HT1B signaling for survival.
Observed in multiple sensitive lines (SNU840, HGC27, MKN1, SNUC5, KYSE510); activating PI3K mutations may create dependence on serotonin receptor-mediated PI3K/AKT crosstalk.
Observed in sensitive lines (HEC265, 786O, FTC133, ZR751); PTEN loss hyperactivates PI3K/AKT, potentially enhancing dependence on HTR1B-mediated survival signals.
Observed in sensitive lines (HEC265, SNUC5, K029AX); BRAF activation may cooperate with serotonin receptor signaling to drive MAPK-dependent survival.
Observed in sensitive lines (BICR6, FTC133); NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK, which may synergize with HTR1B signaling.
Observed in sensitive line HGC27; MET amplification/mutation may drive survival that is sensitive to HTR1B antagonism.
EGFR-mutant lung lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650) are among the least affected, suggesting EGFR activation provides a survival bypass.
KRAS mutations appear in several resistant lines (CL11, GSU, OV7, T3M4), suggesting RAS/MAPK activation may reduce dependence on HTR1B.
SB-216641 has low affinity for HTR1A; high HTR1A expression may compensate for HTR1B blockade and support survival.
SB-216641 is less selective for HTR1D; high HTR1D expression may maintain serotonergic survival signaling despite HTR1B blockade.
TP53 mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so they are not predictive; however, some resistant lines have wild-type TP53, suggesting intact p53 may protect.
Observed in sensitive lines (SNU1214, K029AX); cell cycle deregulation may increase dependence on survival signaling pathways.
